arms.diagnostic_note: Double-bridge perturbation hurts rather than helps within the 2s time limit. The mechanism is sound in theory (non-sequential 4-opt escapes 2-opt local optima), but the overhead of (1) totalCost() O(N) recompute after perturbation, (2) splitting SA time into shorter phases with cold restarts, (3) the perturbed tour needing significant SA time to recover — all exceed the benefit. For N=200K in 2 seconds, maximizing the number of high-quality SA iterations matters more than exploring new basins. The score variance (68.73 to 78.74) suggests timing pressure from double-bridge overhead pushes some test cases over the time limit.

metadata.note: High score variance due to machine load affecting 2s time limit. When timing is favorable, both arms score ~78.8; when load is high, scores drop to 68-74.

arms.diagnostic_note: The ablation confirms that the key improvements are: (1) grid-guided 2-opt neighbor selection, (2) penalty-aware fast delta computation, (3) Or-opt moves, (4) position tracking via pos[] array. These together improve iter-1's score from 69.5 to 78.8. Double-bridge is not a necessary component; in fact it hurts. The real iter-1 code (which the handoff incorrectly described) used random swap + boundary-only approximate 2-opt, scoring ~69.5. The grid-guided + penalty-aware approach is the dominant improvement.

discrepancy_analysis: The iter-2 handoff incorrectly stated iter-1 scored 78.881, but iter-1 actually scored 69.5 with a simpler algorithm (random swap + approximate boundary-only 2-opt). The 78.9 figure may have been from a variant tested during iter-1 exploration but not saved as the official h-main patch. Both iter-2 arms significantly beat the real iter-1 baseline. The main finding is that double-bridge perturbation does NOT help for this problem within the 2s time limit — the overhead outweighs the benefit of exploring new basins. Continuous SA with high-quality moves (grid-guided 2-opt, penalty-aware delta, Or-opt) is optimal. High score variance (±5 points) is caused by machine load affecting the 2-second time limit on the judge.
